title: Human Cost · Iran War
scope_note: Iran-arc theaters only (Iran, Lebanon, US forces). The Iran and Lebanon figures are undifferentiated health-ministry totals — no institution publishes a military/civilian split. The US row differs: it counts individually identified deaths, with wider compilations shown separately.

rows.secondary: 26,500+ injured · UNICEF 31 Jul: 386 children killed, 2,117 injured
rows.note: Attributed to the Foundation of Martyrs and Veterans Affairs, whose page did not retrieve again on 3 September. A UN country page did resolve, carrying a UNICEF figure of 31 July for children only — it does not supersede this total.

rows.secondary: 12,359 wounded · 135 health workers killed since 2 March
rows.note: Health ministry count since 2 March, published 6 September by one Western wire — the first refresh in 94 days after six failures. The separate since-Oct-2023 series is 8,920. The 4,346 figure refused on 7 September, carried only by Chinese state media, was twelve below the ministry's own.

rows.secondary: 19 in the Pentagon database (22 Sep); 22+ per officials (disputed)
rows.note: Four deaths are individually named and incident-verified. The Pentagon's public database reached 19 on 22 September with an Army officer's death en route to the region (Washington Post). Officials told the Post at least 22; Hegseth denies any concealment. The value stays at the identified count.

More than 830 wounded per the Defense Casualty Analysis System, as relayed by AP via The New Arab on 18 September. Earlier: 417 to 30 June (IG report) and 774 in late August (Military Times). The database itself was not read.
rows.secondary: 774 in late August (Military Times); 417 to 30 June (inspector general report)

footnote: "Identified" means every death has a name or a verified incident behind it. "Reported" means a credible outlet published a total nobody has independently confirmed. "Editorial estimate" means we split a total into military and civilian deaths using the published methods of two conflict-monitoring groups, ACLED and AOAV, checked against Reuters, AFP, IRNA and Lebanon’s Health Ministry. Where a figure is out of date, its row note says so. All casualty counts in an active war are contested.
